evals.prompt: I run content for Kibble Crate (example.com), a dog-food subscription service. Another dog-food subscription brand, Bowlful, wrote proposing that we each add the other to a 'recommended resources' box in our blog sidebars, so every post on both sites links to the other. They say it would help both of us rank. How should I answer?
evals.expected_output: A Decline decision with one-line fit-test answers (direct competitor; asks for a sidebar link on every post, which fails both the 'what they want' check and the quality check; no single named page in return), and a filled T4 reply with no placeholders and no em dashes, plus a tracker row.
expectations: Confirms or asks for the client's rules (competitor list, frozen pages, named sender) or states the assumptions used
Classifies Bowlful as a direct competitor and decides Decline
Notes that sitewide or sidebar links fail the quality check even apart from the competitor rule
Uses the T4 template with every placeholder filled, signed with the named sender, no em dashes
Does not offer Bowlful any link or mention on example.com
Logs a tracker row with the five fit-test answers, decision, template sent, date and status

evals.prompt: I look after the blog at Kiln & Glaze (example.com), a pottery-supplies shop. A ceramics hobby site, clayhour.example, emailed asking whether we trade links. They mention our guide 'Choosing your first pottery wheel' as the page they'd like a link from, but they don't say which of their pages would link back to us or where. Nobody else is on the thread yet; I'm replying first. What do I send?
evals.expected_output: A Need details decision: our page is named but nothing on their side is, so the fit test cannot pass yet. A check of whether the wheel guide is frozen or our most-cited page. A filled T2 email used as a first reply (no hand-off clause) that asks only for what is missing: the URL of their page and where the mention would sit.
expectations: Decides Need details: their page is not named, so the Give and Quality checks cannot be run yet
Checks the named guide against the client's rules (frozen pages, most-cited page) before offering it
Uses T2 as a first reply: no hand-off clause and no question about our page, which they already named
Does not agree to any link before their page URL arrives and passes the quality floors
Leaves no placeholder in the email and uses no em dashes

evals.prompt: I want to start a mention exchange for Spokewise (example.com), a bike-repair shop with a blog. There's a cycling site at blog.example.org with an article called 'Fixing a flat on the road' that I think is cited a lot in AI answers. Our 'Tubeless tyre setup guide' at example.com/guides/tubeless is being refreshed this month. Write the outreach email.
evals.expected_output: A fit check of the target page (publisher, not a competitor, live, indexable, on topic, real traffic), verification of the AI-citation claim before using it, and a filled T9 outbound proposal.
expectations: Checks that the cycling site is not a competitor and that the target page is live, indexable and on topic
Verifies that the article is cited in AI answers or ranks for the topic before stating it, instead of inventing a compliment
Uses the T9 template naming their page title and our page title and URL
Offers a reference in return and ends with a yes/no question
Notes the next steps: log the thread, confirm both sides with T6 on acceptance, and check both links are live and in the main text before closing with T7

evals.prompt: Lenslocker (example.com) rents out camera gear. A photography school, shutterclass.example, wants a link to their beginners' course from our pricing page. In return they'd add us to their article 'Renting vs buying your first camera' (they sent the URL; it gets steady search traffic). Our pricing page has no editorial content and we don't put outbound links there. What's the decision and the email?
evals.expected_output: A Counter decision: the school sells a service the brand does not sell and offers a named, relevant page, but the pricing page is the wrong page. A filled T3 email offering two content pages that fit (for example a beginner camera guide being updated) and asking which page they would link from and the sentence they suggest.
expectations: Decides Counter, not Accept and not Decline
Explains that the requested page is the wrong place for the link
Runs the quality check on the school's named page (live, indexable, on topic, real traffic, link in the main text)
Uses the T3 template offering content pages that are being updated, not the most-cited page
Leaves no placeholder in the email and uses no em dashes
